source.title: Entropy-SGD: biasing gradient descent into wide valleys
source.authors: Pratik Chaudhari; A. Choromańska; Stefano Soatto; Yann LeCun; Carlo Baldassi; C. Borgs; J. Chayes; Levent Sagun; R. Zecchina

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses the idea that flat or wide valleys may generalize well to motivate Entropy-SGD, but its own experiments evaluate that new optimizer against SGD or Adam rather than test a listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports Entropy-SGD benchmark comparisons, but those are results of its own new optimization method and do not test a listed version. The Hessian or Fisher-spectrum measurements are recorded below; they do not measure the magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or training-test gap relationship specified by V7.
record.test_reason: Section 5.2 reports the study's own MNIST results for convolutional and fully connected networks trained with the same Adam baseline recipe. These bear directly on V3, independently of the proposed optimizer's performance. The Hessian measurements do not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors report predominantly flat local geometry across the examined networks and introduce Entropy-SGD to favor wide valleys. They find comparable held-out performance, lower training cross-entropy, and substantially faster training for recurrent networks, with relatively minor timing gains for convolutional networks.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces Entropy-SGD, using inner stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics to estimate a local-entropy gradient; benchmark comparisons use different training procedures and do not test a listed version.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that momentum tuning was crucial for good RNN results; CNN experiments used momentum 0.9, while PTB-LSTM Entropy-SGD used 0.5 and char-LSTM Entropy-Adam used β1 = 0.5.

fits_no_version.finding: The measured spectra have large near-zero components across the small networks; All-CNN-BN uses a diagonal empirical Fisher proxy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Several trained networks have predominantly near-zero local curvature directions, alongside relatively few directions with larger curvature.

record.problems: The paper states that exact Hessians were computed only for the first three, smaller networks; All-CNN-BN uses a diagonal empirical Fisher proxy. The reported spectrum measurements do not pair the specified magnitude-aware sharpness measure with training-test gaps.
record.rows_left_out: Entropy-SGD versus SGD or Adam benchmark outcomes in Sections 5.2–5.4 and Appendix C.1 were left out because they evaluate the paper's new method rather than a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
The contribution of local connectivity, learning sparse local connections, convolutional initialization of fully connected networks, and datasets beyond MNIST.
A comparable adaptive-optimizer versus SGD experiment under specified tuning regimes. The proposed optimizer comparisons and separately configured Hessian experiments do not establish this.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
The effect of dropout itself. MNIST dropout changes accompany optimizer changes and do not isolate its effect.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with training-test gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Add the MNIST architectural comparison under the shared Adam baseline: mnistfc error 1.39 ± 0.03% versus LeNet error 0.51 ± 0.01%, five independent runs, 100 epochs, dropout probability 0.5 after each layer. These baseline results test V3 and are not covered by the stated omission of new-optimizer comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The architectural comparison supports V3 without identifying local connectivity as the cause: the architectures also differ in other respects, including batch normalization. The study is not an original source for V3.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error across widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance under the stated comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning regimes; Entropy-Adam is not a test of this comparison.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets.
The effect of adding or removing dropout under the stated regimes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, comparison with norm- and margin-based measures, and correlation with training-test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: small-LeNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured Hessian eigenspectrum at a local minimum after training with Adam.
rows.measure: Approximately 94% of directions had near-zero eigenvalues (magnitude less than 10−4).
rows.note: Measures Hessian spectrum, not magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or the training-test gap.
rows.check: The approximately 94% near-zero Hessian eigenvalues are correctly reported but measure neither magnitude-aware sharpness nor its relationship with generalization gaps.

rows.subject: small-mnistfc
rows.size_stated: 50,890 parameters; one layer of 32 hidden units
rows.operation_detail: Measured Hessian eigenspectrum at local minima after training with momentum-based SGD.
rows.note: The result describes near-zero curvature; it does not report the V7 measure or training-test gap.
rows.check: The 90% refers to Hessian eigenvalues, not Hessian matrix entries. This spectrum does not test any listed version.

rows.subject: All-CNN-BN
rows.operation_detail: Used the diagonal empirical Fisher information as a proxy for Hessian eigenvalues at a local minimum.
rows.note: The paper uses a Fisher diagonal proxy rather than an exact Hessian here; it does not report the V7 measure or training-test gap.

relationships.condition: MNIST; LeNet with batch normalization versus a fully connected network with two 1024-unit hidden layers; Adam baseline training for 100 epochs.
relationships.reason: Section 5.2 reports error of 0.51 ± 0.01% for LeNet versus 1.39 ± 0.03% for mnistfc over five runs; this verdict uses the text because the architectural results have no extracted row.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower LeNet test error under Adam remains unverified.
